summary: This bill amends the Clean Air Act to exempt marginal oil and gas wells (those averaging 15 barrels of oil or 90,000 cubic feet of gas per day or less) from all EPA performance standards, monitoring, reporting, leak detection, and related requirements under section 111, requires the EPA to revise its rules within 180 days and drop pending enforcement actions, and mandates quick approval of state plans that drop such requirements for these wells.

scores.thoughts: The bill makes no reference to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations of any kind. It solely addresses regulatory exemptions under the Clean Air Act.
No provisions in the bill address taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue measures.
The legislation has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No content relates to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill contains nothing concerning immigration, borders, or visas.
No provisions touch on reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not address military or defense spending or policy.

The core purpose of the bill is to exempt low-production 'marginal' oil and gas wells from Clean Air Act standards of performance, monitoring, leak detection, and related EPA requirements. This directly limits environmental regulations on the oil and gas sector to benefit small domestic producers.
